description: A destructuring assignment reads its source the same way a binding pattern does, so `({ value: out } = box)` consults the get half and the data property beside it stays clean. A shorthand's default is a read of `box.value`, not a write to it — mistaking the two would consult the clean setter and lose the diagnostic.

diagnostics.message: Destructuring `value: out` escapes this `@nothrow` function: it runs the getter `value`, whose body was analyzed and can throw. Your outs: bridge it with `try`/`catch`, or make the getter `value` non-throwing — mark it `@nothrow` and the escapes inside it are reported too.

Reading `box.value` escapes this `@nothrow` function: it runs the getter `value`, whose body was analyzed and can throw. Your outs: bridge it with `try`/`catch`, or make the getter `value` non-throwing — mark it `@nothrow` and the escapes inside it are reported too.
